qualifying_findings.source_title: Context Engineering: An Interactive Guide to How AI Agents Work
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The guide explains context windows, agent loops, context rot, compaction, memory, and loop engineering as parts of how agents build and maintain working context.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: It reinforces that durable agent instructions, open files, tool outputs, compaction, and persisted memory are operational context surfaces that need explicit management rather than ad hoc prompt stuffing.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Useful for context-architecture pages about context selection, compaction, memory boundaries, and loop-aware request packages.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: During ingest, compare against existing leaves on context selection, compaction, and durable instructions before creating any new page.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Your SDLC is your context engineering
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The article argues that an agent's useful context is the SDLC itself, not only repository instruction files. It emphasizes task-level builder/reviewer separation, planning quality, and weekly learning loops for teams adopting agents.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: It maps context engineering from file-level instructions to lifecycle design: specification gates, task slicing, independent review, and escalation boundaries become part of the context supplied to agents.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Candidate evidence for downstream-owned operating-model guidance on specification-first agent work, task-level reviewer separation, and adoption feedback loops.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: If ingested, keep vendor and company references as upstream-owned routing metadata and focus local synthesis on SDLC-as-context practice.

qualifying_findings.source_title: AI Software Testing Skills for Smarter QA Automation
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The page describes reusable software-testing skills for AI agents, including test-suite architecture, test-driven development, HTTP load profiling, vulnerability auditing, open-source skill installation, customization, and review of generated outputs.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: It is a current vendor example of packaging testing and QA workflows as reusable agent skills, with explicit customization and human review steps.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Supports local pages about portable agent skills, AI-assisted TDD, QA skill review boundaries, and skill-install risk where third-party repositories are pulled into an agent environment.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: During ingest, separate local practice evidence from Kimi product coverage and evaluate whether package-install risk belongs under governance-and-risk.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Context Engineering for Agentic Applications on AWS Bedrock AgentCore and MongoDB Atlas
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The post frames production agent reliability as explicit context assembly across identity, task state, memory, retrieved knowledge, tool outputs, and governance controls, with scale, cost, observability, and bounded context as production concerns.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: It ties context engineering to production harness design: agent routing, retrieval scope, memory, state, governance, cost control, and observability need to be engineered as one request lifecycle.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Candidate evidence for local application-pattern and retrieval/tool pages that describe context assembly as a governed harness responsibility.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Avoid duplicating AWS or MongoDB product coverage; keep only the practice pattern around controlled context assembly.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Using the GitHub Copilot SDK for Java
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The article describes a Java SDK for creating agent sessions, registering tools, sending prompts, receiving structured responses, streaming real-time events, customizing system messages, using BYOK providers, and opting in only to needed tools.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: It offers a concrete current example of harness-owned tool schemas, structured outputs, progress streaming, server-side agent sessions, and least-capability tool exposure.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Useful for local harness architecture, structured-output, streaming-progress, tool-registration, and permissions guidance without creating product encyclopedia coverage.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: During ingest, compare with application-harness-patterns, agent-harness-components, and user-visible-progress-and-runtime-telemetry.
